results.caption: “Come break dogs with me in 100° weather.” 😂 When people think about dog training, they usually picture the lessons, behavior modification, off-leash work, or before & after transformations. What they don’t see is this. In between training sessions, client calls, virtual consultations, and everything else that comes with running a business, I’m out here doing potty rotations 3-4 times a day for every dog in my care. This is the current crew of dogs here for boarding and board & train. Some are here for basic obedience, some are here for serious behavioral work, and some need a little more time and management than others. No matter why they’re here, they all get time to get out, stretch their legs, use the bathroom, decompress, and just be dogs. Days like today are a good reminder that dog care isn’t just about training. It’s about paying attention. 100 degree heat can become dangerous fast, especially for certain breeds, ages, and personalities. Knowing how to read a dog’s body language, recognize the early signs of heat stress, and adjust accordingly is just as important as teaching a sit or down. The reality is that a lot of dog training is repetitive. It’s cleaning, walking, rotating dogs, managing schedules, and doing the little things consistently every single day.  But somewhere in that repetition, you build relationships. You learn each dog’s quirks, personalities, and routines. And honestly, that’s one of my favorite parts of the job. Most people see the finished product. The calm walk. The obedience. The transformation. What they don’t see are the hundreds of small moments that make it possible. Before watching this, what did you think a dog trainer spent most of their day doing? #dogtraining #dogtrainer #dogs #dogsoftiktok #dog

results.caption:
Are your routines making you... slower? 👀 #ad

Four routines I’ve been following for years that have helped me become a better runner and yes, hydration with @goultima is one of them.

Which one are you going to be more intentional about this week?
results.transcript: Runners who often make the biggest gains are the ones dialing in their routines in between runs. Getting enough sleep. I know this is a no-brainer, but getting consistent sleep can be hard, especially if you're a working professional, have a busy personal life, or have kids. Aiming for a minimum of 78 hours of sleep per night allows the brain and body to rest and recover. Hydration, hydration, hydration. And not just water. It's also good to incorporate electrolytes in your everyday routine. That's why I use Ultima. It has six key electrolytes to support everyday hydration. Plus, it contains zero calories, zero carbs, and zero sugar. Fueling before and after your training. Your muscles use glycogen, which is a stored form of carbohydrate, for energy. Eating carbs before a training session helps you top off those stores, while eating carbs and protein after a workout not only helps you replenish your glycogen, but also supports muscle repair. Keep your easy runs easy. Now, I know it's not easy. However, just think about it. If all your workouts are hard, that means fatigue is building faster than fitness. What you want is those easy runs to help you build your aerobic base while keeping you fresh for your hardest workouts. So remember, it's the small and easy routine to add up over time. This week, pick one routine you want to improve, and let me know what it is in the comments below.
